newsitem.title: UK: UK minister to be grilled by MPs over sleaze probe.
newsitem.headline: UK minister to be grilled by MPs over sleaze probe.

text.p: In another headache for Prime Minister John Major, parliament's Standards and Privileges Committee on Tuesday summoned junior minister Andrew Mitchell to explain his role in an earlier probe into allegations of sleaze involving ex-trade minister Neil Hamilton.
The committee said Mitchell, a junior social security minister, would answer questions in public next Monday at 1700 GMT.

One minister, David Willetts, was forced to resign last month after being strongly criticised by the Standards and Privileges Committee for not being "frank and open" when he gave evidence to the committee.

The panel was probing whether Willetts, when he was a "whip" or government business manager, in 1994 improperly tried to influence a panel of MPs probing allegations that Hamilton had accepted cash in return for asking questions in parliament.

Mitchell, also a former whip, became embroiled in the affair, when Labour's Dale Campbell-Savours showed the committee a letter that he said showed Mitchell had also tried improperly to influence the inquiry.
